Jack Nicklaus. The Golden Bear. An American professional golfer who won 18 major championships—the most by any player until Tiger Woods approached the record—establishing himself as perhaps the greatest player of golf's modern era. His 46-year career, spanning from 1962 to 2005, demonstrated unparalleled consistency and dominance across five decades.

He won 18 major championships across all four majors: 6 Masters, 5 US Opens, 3 Open Championships, and 4 PGA Championships. He finished second in major championships a record 19 times, showing remarkable consistency in contending for titles. Nicklaus won his first professional major, the 1962 US Open at Oakmont, unseating Arnold Palmer in a playoff, signaling a generational shift. At age 46 in 1986, he captured the Masters, making him the oldest winner of a major championship. He pioneered modern course management and strategic golf, emphasizing precision and course design knowledge.

Beyond his playing career, Nicklaus designed over 300 golf courses worldwide, creating a second career as a golf architect. As an amateur golfer in spirit, though technically professional, he achieved the Grand Slam by winning all four major championships in 1966. Tiger Woods is the only player to rival or exceed his major championship record. Gary Player competed with him throughout the 1960s and 1970s, and Tom Watson emerged as a younger rival during Nicklaus's later competitive years.
